title: Probing hot spots of protein-protein interactions mediated by the safety-belt region of REV7.
authors: Dash, Radha Charan; Arianna, Gianluca A; Patel, Seema M; Rizzo, Alessandro A; Harrahill, Noah J; Korzhnev, Dmitry M; Hadden, M Kyle
one_liner_zh: 该文通过计算分析REV7蛋白与RBM肽段的蛋白-蛋白互作界面热点，虽非TF-DNA体系，但涉及结合界面建模与实验验证，方法可迁移至蛋白-DNA互作研究。
abstract: REV7 is a HORMA (Hop1, Rev7, Mad2) family adaptor protein best known as an accessory subunit of the translesion synthesis (TLS) DNA polymerase zeta (Polzeta). In this role, REV7 binds REV3, the catalytic subunit of Polzeta, by locking REV7-binding motifs (RBMs) in REV3 underneath the REV7 safety-belt loop. The same mechanism is used by REV7 to interact with RBMs from other proteins in DNA damage response (DDR) and mitosis. Because of the importance of REV7 for TLS and other DDR pathways, targeting REV7:RBM protein-protein interactions (PPIs) with small molecules has emerged as a strategy to enhance cancer response to genotoxic chemotherapy. To identify druggable pockets at the REV7:RBM interface, we performed computational analyses of REV7 complexed with several RBM partners. The contributions of different interface regions to REV7:RBM stabilization were corroborated experimentally. These studies provide insights into key intermolecular interactions and establish targetable regions of REV7 for the design of REV7:RBM PPI inhibitors.
abstract_zh: REV7是一种HORMA（Hop1、Rev7、Mad2）家族衔接蛋白，最著名的是作为跨损伤合成（TLS）DNA聚合酶zeta（Polzeta）的辅助亚基。在此角色中，REV7通过将REV3（Polzeta的催化亚基）中的REV7结合基序（RBMs）锁定在REV7安全腰带环下方来结合REV3。REV7利用相同机制与DNA损伤应答（DDR）和有丝分裂中其他蛋白的RBMs相互作用。由于REV7在TLS及其他DDR通路中的重要性，用小分子靶向REV7:RBM蛋白-蛋白相互作用（PPIs）已成为增强癌症对基因毒性化疗反应的一种策略。为识别REV7:RBM界面上的可成药口袋，我们对REV7与多个RBM伙伴的复合物进行了计算分析。不同界面区域对REV7:RBM稳定化的贡献通过实验得到证实。这些研究提供了对关键分子间相互作用的见解，并确定了REV7上可用于设计REV7:RBM PPI抑制剂的可靶向区域。
